text: Amongst the following statements, that which was not proposed by Dalton was :
options:
Chemical reactions involve reorganization of atoms. These are neither created nor destroyed in
a chemical reaction.

When gases combine or are produced in a chemical reaction they do so in a simple ratio by
volume provided all gases are at the same T & P.
All the atoms of a given element have identical properties including identical mass. Atoms of different elements differ in mass.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
Dalton's atomic theory states that matter consists of indivisible atoms; all atoms of a given element have identical properties including identical mass, while atoms of different elements differ in mass; compounds form when atoms of different elements combine in a fixed ratio; and chemical reactions involve only reorganisation of atoms, which are neither created nor destroyed.

Statements (A), (B) and (D) are therefore postulates of Dalton's theory.

Statement (C), that gases combine or are produced in a simple ratio by volume at the same temperature and pressure, is Gay-Lussac's law of gaseous volumes, which Dalton did not propose.

Hence, the correct option is (C).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text: The theory that can completely/properly explain the nature of bonding in [$Ni(CO)_{4}$] is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In $[\mathrm{Ni}(\mathrm{CO}){}_{4}]$ each CO donates its carbon lone pair into an empty orbital of Ni ($σ$ bond), and filled Ni $d$ orbitals donate electron density back into the empty $π^{\ast }$ orbitals of CO ($π$ back-bond).

This synergic bonding strengthens the Ni–C bond and weakens the C–O bond, so the C–O bond is longer and its stretching frequency lower than in free CO.

Valence bond theory gives only the $sp^{3}$ hybridisation, tetrahedral shape and diamagnetism; it has no description of $π$ back-donation. Crystal field theory treats ligands as point charges and cannot explain why neutral CO is a strong-field ligand, and Werner's theory deals only with primary and secondary valencies.

Molecular orbital theory combines the metal orbitals with the CO $σ$ and $π^{\ast }$ orbitals, so it accounts for both the $σ$ donation and the $π$ back-bonding and explains the bonding completely.

Hence, the correct option is (D).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
At $35^{o}C$, the vapour pressure of $CS_{2}$
 is 512 mm. Hg and that of acetone is 344 mm Hg. A solution
of $CS_{2}$
 in acetone has a total vapour pressure of 600 mm Hg. The false statement amongst the
following is :
options: $CS_{2}$ and acetone are less attracted to each other than to themselves.
a mixture of $100 ml. CS_{2}$ and 100 ml. acetone has a volume < 200 ml.
Heat must be absorbed in order to produce the solution at $35^{o}C$
Raoult's law is not obeyed by this system.
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
As the vapour pressure of mixture increases so the force of attraction of mixture is less than the individual component.

Since the vapour pressure of the solution is
greater than individual vapour pressure of both
pure components, the solution shows a
positive deviation from Raoult’s law.

$\therefore$ $\Delta_{Sol}$H $>$ 0 

As $\Delta_{Sol}$H $>$ 0 then solution is endothermic.

 and here $\Delta_{Sol}$ Volume $>$ 0. As $\Delta_{Sol}$ Volume $>$ 0 then a mixture of $100 ml. CS_{2}$ and 100 ml. acetone has a volume more than 200 ml. It happens because the distance between molecules increases due to force of attraction of mixture decreases.
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text:
A solution of m-chloroaniline, m-chlorophenol and m-chlorobenzoic acid in ethyl acetate was extracted initially with a saturated solution of NaHCO$_{3}$
 to give fraction A. The left over organic phase
was extracted with dilute NaOH solution to give fraction B. The final organic layer was labelled as
fraction C. Fractions A,B and C, contain respectively :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
m-Chlorobenzoic acid ($\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a}}\approx 3.8$) is a stronger acid than carbonic acid, so saturated $\mathrm{NaHCO}{}_{3}$ converts it into water-soluble sodium m-chlorobenzoate, while m-chlorophenol ($\mathrm{p}K_{\mathrm{a}}\approx 9$) is too weak an acid to react. Fraction A therefore contains m-chlorobenzoic acid.

Dilute $\mathrm{NaOH}$ is a strong enough base to convert m-chlorophenol into water-soluble sodium m-chlorophenoxide, so fraction B contains m-chlorophenol.

m-Chloroaniline is a base and reacts with neither alkali, so it stays in the ethyl acetate layer as fraction C.

Hence, the correct option is (B).
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text: Two solutions, A and B, each of 100L was made by dissolving 4g of NaOH and 9.8 g of $H_{2}SO_{4}$ in water, respectively. The pH of the resultant solution obtained from mixing 40L of solution A and 10L of solution B is :
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
In 100 L solution  $H_{2}SO_{4}$ present = 9.8 gm

$\therefore$ In 10 L solution  $H_{2}SO_{4}$ present = $9.8\times \frac{10}{100}$ gm

$\Rightarrow$ In 10 L solution moles of  $H_{2}SO_{4}$ present = $\frac{9.8}{98}\times \frac{10}{100}$

In one molecule of $H_{2}SO_{4}$ two $H^{+}$ ion present.

$\therefore$ In 10 L solution moles of  $H^{+}$ present = 2$\times\frac{9.8}{98}\times \frac{10}{100}$ = 0.02 moles

Also In 100 L solution NaOH present = 4 gm

$\therefore$ In 40 L solution  NaOH present = $4\times \frac{40}{100}$

$\Rightarrow$ In 40 L solution moles of NaOH present = $\frac{4}{40}\times \frac{40}{100}$

In one molecule of NaOH one $OH^{-}$ ion present.

$\therefore$ In 40 L solution moles of $OH^{-}$ ion present = $\frac{4}{40}\times \frac{40}{100}$ = 0.04 moles

As moles of $OH^{-}$ ion is more than $H^{+}$ ion, so solution is basic.

$\therefore$ Final Conc. of $OH^{–} =$ $\frac{0.04-0.02}{40+10}$ = 4 $\times$ $10^{-4}$

$\therefore$ pOH $= – \log  (4 ×10^{–4}) = 3.4$

pH = 14 – 3.4 = 10.6
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot

text: During the nuclear explosion, one of the products is $^{90}Sr$ with half life of 6.93 years. If 1 $μ$ g of $^{90}Sr$ was absorbed in the bones of newly born baby in place of Ca, how much time, in years, is required to reduce it by 90% if it is not lost metabolically?
sourceReference: NTA JEE Main JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot via ExamSIDE (questions.examside.com)

solution.body:
All nuclear decays follow first order kinetics

t = $\frac{1}{k}\ln \frac{[A_{0}]}{[A]}$

= $\frac{\left (t_{1/2}\right )}{0.693}\times 2.303\log _{10}10$

= 10 × 2.303 × 1

= 23.03 years

Shortcut Method :

$t_{90$%} = $\frac{10}{3}\times t_{50%}$

= $\frac{10}{3}\times 6.93$ = 23.1
sourceReferences: ExamSIDE explanation for JEE Main 2020 (Online) 7th January Morning Slot
